synopsis: NHTSA’s New Car Assessment Program provides consumer ratings using AEB tests at 40–80 km/h; its test values are consumer-assessment values, not law [f15430, f2541]. It does not regulate a quarry loader, haul truck, excavator or dozer merely because that machine has automatic braking [f2514]. Stationary and moving lead-vehicle tests begin at 40 km/h and increase in 10 km/h steps to 80 km/h while no contact occurs; contact ends the series [f2539]. The lead-vehicle-decelerating test family uses headways of 12–40 m and target decelerations of 0.3–0.5 g [f2540]. The final decision notice was signed in November 2024 and appeared in the Federal Register on 3 December 2024 [f2538].

relations.note: Specifies speed increments, lead-vehicle scenarios and contact-based stopping rule for the glossary’s test range.
Clarifies that consumer-rating test values are not law.
Adds headway and target-deceleration parameters for another AEB test family.
Nonlegal consumer-assessment status supports excluding NCAP as an automatic source of off-road regulation.
